card.name: The word are in 'alternative treatment options are inadequate'
card.fires_on: The verb 'are' right after 'alternative treatment options' in the opioid boxed warning about using opioids with benzodiazepines or other CNS depressants only when other options are inadequate. Weaker on 'is' after 'if the drug' in addiction warnings.

modes.label: Reserve-for-inadequate-options clause
modes.description: The verb 'are' after 'alternative treatment options', just before 'inadequate'.
modes.example: for use in patients for whom alternative treatment options<< are>> inadequate [ see Warnings and Preca

modes.label: Drug is misused
modes.description: The verb 'is' after 'if the drug' in an addiction-risk sentence.
modes.example: Addiction can occur at recommended dosages and if the drug<< is>> misused or abused.

card.plain: It marks the spot in the opioid warning where the text says other treatments 'are' inadequate, a very repeated phrase.
